_provenance.source: Apache Cassandra 5.0.2 serializer source (docker image cassandra:5.0.2; sources fetched from github.com/apache/cassandra tag cassandra-5.0.2).

framing_contract.collection_size: CollectionSerializer.writeCollectionSize == ByteBuffer.putInt(elements); sizeOfCollectionSize == TypeSizes.INT_SIZE == 4. Fixed 4-byte big-endian SIGNED int. NOT a VInt for the frozen/CQL-protocol (ByteBufferAccessor) serialized form.
framing_contract.element_size: CollectionSerializer.writeValue == output.putInt(size); -1 == null. Fixed 4-byte big-endian SIGNED int prefix per element value (and per map value).
framing_contract.set_order: SetSerializer.serializeValues sorts the serialized element buffers with comparators.buffer (Cassandra byte-comparable SORT order). For text (UTF8Type) the buffer order equals lexicographic UTF-8 byte order.
framing_contract.map_order: MapSerializer/AbstractMapSerializer keep entries key-sorted (by key buffer comparator). getIndexFromSerialized skips the value buffer when comparison<0 (hasValues==true).
framing_contract.set_lookup: SetSerializer.getSerializedValue linear-scans; returns the matching value buffer; short-circuits to null once comparison>0 (sorted-order). Element value at byte offset = sizeOfCollectionSize + sum over preceding elements of (4 + len_j); readValue slices [offset+4, offset+4+len].
framing_contract.index_lookup: AbstractMapSerializer.getIndexFromSerialized returns the ELEMENT INDEX i (0-based, not a byte offset) of a matching key, or -1 if absent; short-circuits to -1 once comparison>0.
framing_contract.range: AbstractMapSerializer.getIndexesRangeFromSerialized returns a half-open Range.closedOpen(start, end) i.e. [start,end). from/to UNSET => start=0 / end=n. If from is greater than every element => Range.closedOpen(0,0) (empty). end defaults to n if to is past the last element.

vint_element_count_contract.note: The MULTI-CELL on-disk SSTable collection path reads the element/cell count with the Cassandra unsigned VInt (org.apache.cassandra.utils.VIntCoding / DataInputPlus.readUnsignedVInt). CQLite implements this as parser::vint::parse_vuint / encode_vuint. Size classes: leading-ones in byte 0 select extra-byte count; unsigned VInt of value v occupies ceil((bits_needed)/7)-style class boundaries at 2^7,2^14,2^21,... The frozen-collection serializer above uses a fixed 4-byte int instead and is unaffected by these boundaries.
vint_element_count_contract.source: org/apache/cassandra/utils/VIntCoding.java; org/apache/cassandra/io/util/DataInputPlus.readUnsignedVInt(); confirmed in CQLite read path row_decoder:6821 (parse_vuint).

cqlite_reader_framing.note: CQLite's no-heuristics schema reader (parser::types::parse_list_with_schema / parse_map_with_schema) decodes the MULTI-CELL on-disk SSTable form, NOT the frozen 4-byte ByteBuffer form. In that form the element COUNT and each element LENGTH PREFIX are Cassandra SIGNED VInts (parser::vint::encode_vint / parse_vint, zigzag), and -1 length == null. For a `text` element the length-prefixed bytes are themselves a `parse_text` buffer == [signed-VInt str_len][utf8]; for `int` the element is 4 raw big-endian bytes (parse_int). The 4-byte-BE-int `serialized_bytes` vectors below are the FROZEN/CQL-protocol (CollectionSerializer ByteBufferAccessor) form used to validate Cassandra's offset/lookup/range ARITHMETIC; the reader-decode tests rebuild the same logical members in the VInt form. Both framings must yield identical ordered members (single_cell_multicell_equivalence).

set_lookup_offsets.description: Frozen set<text> {alpha,bravo,delta} already in Cassandra sort order. Verifies element value byte-ranges, lookup-by-element returns the right index, and an ABSENT element ('charlie') returns no match WITHOUT shifting the byte offsets of the surrounding present elements.

lookups.comment: absent; sorts between bravo and delta; short-circuits after delta>charlie path. Present-element offsets must be unchanged.
absent; greater than all; short-circuits to -1.
absent; less than all; first comparison>0 => -1 immediately.

set_range_offsets.description: getIndexesRangeFromSerialized half-open [start,end) semantics over the same {alpha,bravo,delta} set.

ranges.comment: from sorts between bravo/delta -> first element >= charlie is delta(2)
from greater than all => empty closedOpen(0,0)

map_key_lookup_offsets.description: Frozen map<text,int> {alpha:1, bravo:2, delta:3} key-sorted. int values are 4-byte BE. Verifies getIndexFromSerialized returns the ENTRY INDEX (not byte offset), value byte-ranges, and absent-key short-circuit. int values chosen non-negative so byte order is irrelevant (keys drive ordering).

map_key_range_offsets.description: getIndexesRangeFromSerialized over map keys {alpha,bravo,delta}; entry indexes [start,end).

vint_element_count_boundaries.description: Unsigned VInt element-count size-class boundaries for the MULTI-CELL on-disk collection path (Cassandra readUnsignedVInt / CQLite parse_vuint, encode_vuint). Each entry gives the count value, the exact authoritative encoded bytes, and the byte width Cassandra emits.

single_cell_multicell_equivalence.description: A frozen (single-cell) set and a multi-cell set with the SAME members in the SAME Cassandra sort order must decode to the same ordered element sequence. The frozen single-cell wire form is the CollectionSerializer 4-byte-framed blob (one cell value). The multi-cell form stores each element in its own complex cell (element count via unsigned VInt, element bytes in the cell PATH). This vector asserts the ORDERED member list is identical; it does not assert the two wire layouts are byte-identical (they are intentionally different framings).

list_insertion_order.description: Lists (ListType) preserve INSERTION order and are NOT sorted (contrast with set_lookup_offsets, which is sorted). An intentionally non-sorted member sequence [delta, alpha, bravo] must decode back verbatim, positionally. Exercises the same multi-cell reader path as sets but proves the list ordering contract. Decoded via CQLite's MULTI-CELL VInt framing (see cqlite_reader_framing).
